clue.text: What can make us sad all over the country?

indicators.note: the clue asks which word could be rearranged to produce the phrase sad all over, so those three words are the letters to shuffle

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about what could make a whole nation miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What can make' signals that the letters of SAD ALL OVER are rearranged; 'us' is just part of the surface question.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is a Central American nation, so it fits a straightforward description as a country.

clue.text: Ring cops with names originally involved

explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' is surface padding; the fodder is COPS plus NAMES in full.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to surround or circle it, the verb sense of enclose.

clue.text: Quick vehicles going the wrong way

clue.text: Solution I spot could be one adopted by meditators

clue.text: Crack in a dry drain not closed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fissure but is a go, a try.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a crack at something is to have a try at it.

clue.text: Townie finding work papers amongst rubbish

parts.note: OP, short for opus, means a work

indicators.note: amongst means the word for papers goes inside the word for rubbish

explanation.walkthrough: At Eton College, a pupil boarding in town rather than in college is called this; it also means a town-dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweller in a town, from the Latin word for town, so it suits a townsperson.

clue.text: Ring selection from multiple-choice

indicators.note: a selection from the words is a short run of their letters taken out, so the answer sits inside multiple-choice

explanation.surface: A telephone call picked from options on an exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring is to resound or reverberate, which is what a sound does when it echoes back.

clue.text: Drug put in squash, ending in enormous fuss over soft drink

indicators.note: the letter for the drug is put inside the word for squash

explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the fruit drink but is the verb cram; 'over' in a down clue signals turning the fuss word round.

clue.text: Head off relatively fiery creature

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word for relatively fiery is removed

clue.text: Singer's sex appeal shown by line in film

indicators.note: the letter for line is placed inside the word for film

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or coating, a coat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is not a movie but a thin covering, a coat.

clue.text: Initially profits and sales slip after losing one order

explanation.definitionFit: A precept is a rule or command, so it is an order in the sense of an instruction.

clue.text: Near miss quite spoiled horsemanship

clue.text: Warm spell in 2000 possibly

explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the year's hottest season brings warm weather, so a warm spell at that time of year.

clue.text: Party nominators negotiated acceptable emergency solution

clue.text: Gauge ways one may enter trivial conversation

clue.text: Short novel on list upset member of exam team

clue.text: A piece of cake that's clearly fresh

clue.text: Wasted time on each meal

clue.text: In diner before closing I beat up crank

clue.text: Kicking bucket in a rage is no good

clue.text: Dramatist under pressure, it's said, when impatient
